prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: Business software subscription pricing (language en).
Grid: 6 columns × 8 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Merged cells: "Plan" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Price" spans 2 col × 1 row; "Minimum seats" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Contract" spans 1 col × 2 row; "Support" spans 1 col × 2 row.
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Plan" · longest unbreakable word 75px · one-line width 75px
  col 2: header "Price › List price" · longest unbreakable word 37px · one-line width 67px
  col 3: header "Price › Billing terms" · longest unbreakable word 86px · one-line width 490px
  col 4: header "Minimum seats" · longest unbreakable word 66px · one-line width 109px
  col 5: header "Contract" · longest unbreakable word 63px · one-line width 123px
  col 6: header "Support" · longest unbreakable word 79px · one-line width 195px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 360px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A procurement/comparison reference: pick a plan (row) and read its price, how it is billed, seat minimums, contract and support terms. It is scanned vertically by plan and compared horizontally by attribute.","reading":"Reader anchors on column 1 (Plan), reads the bold price, then the billing-terms sentence that explains it, then the three short constraint/attribute columns (seats, contract, support) as a quick checklist. So the eye moves plan → price pair → terms strip, and column 3's long prose is the one cell that must wrap.","groups":["cols 2+3 (Price group): 'List price' is the number, 'Billing terms' its explanation — they must stay adjacent under the merged 'Price' header and be read as a pair","cols 4,5,6 (Minimum seats / Contract / Support): same role — short attribute values in a checklist strip; they should share a similar, compact rhythm even if their headers are narrower than one line","col 1 (Plan) stands alone as row identity and needs a clean, uninterrupted edge"],"keep_intact":["Plan names (Education = 75px) — never split a row identifier","Currency amounts ($12, $45) and the price column header 'List price' (67px)","Numeric seat values in 'Minimum seats'","Short contract/support values and their header words if any scroll budget exists"],"may_wrap":["Billing terms prose (490px one-line) — the natural flexible column; 2–6 lines are acceptable and absorb row-height growth","'Minimum seats', 'Contract', 'Support' headers into two lines if width forces it","Billing-terms header word 'Billing' only as a last resort"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[96,58,100,35,35,35],"idea":"Everything on one 359px screen: Plan and List price keep their full word width, the long Billing-terms prose wraps into a tall narrow column, and the three attribute headers are sacrificed to split words in narrow strips."},{"name":"B","widths":[96,58,107,87,84,100],"idea":"No word ever splits: every header and plan name stays intact, Billing terms wraps to ~6 lines, and the reader scrolls a modest ~170px to reach the attribute strip."},{"name":"C","widths":[96,88,250,130,144,216],"idea":"Natural-width reading: give every column its one-line content width so rows stay shallow and scannable, let only Billing terms wrap to 2–3 lines, and accept a wide ~2.5-screen horizontal scroll."}]}
